label: D1 after S2 rewarded, larger early in episode and after earlier S2 non-reward
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (tv("state", -3) == 2) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp(-ep_trial/10) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * tv("belief", -1)
explanation: Sparse feature that fires only at D1, almost only when the previous trial reached S2 and was rewarded (a1 S2 r or a2 S2 r). It is zero at GO and D2. Its magnitude in that context is larger early in the episode (exp(-ep_trial/10) has the biggest weight, on top of a timing baseline that already decays across deciles). It is larger when the S2 reward is surprising: two trials back was S2 unrewarded (+0.13), three trials back S2 unrewarded (+0.06), and the prior belief that S1 was good before the last trial is high (+0.11). It is smaller when two trials back was S1 rewarded (-0.05) and when the last choice was a1, i.e. the S2 reward came after a rare transition (-0.08). So it reads like an early-episode surprise or update signal for an S2 reward. Absolute belief confidence adds nothing. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.275 (dev 0.28), above the profile all-observed reference of 0.18 but below the all ceiling of 0.45. The model value decile alone reaches 0.26, so the observed-only terms roughly match what the earlier value/policy explanation got. Most of the variance among S2-rewarded D1 steps (fire about 0.5 or stay silent) is still unexplained. Partially explained: the context is clear but the magnitude fit is under 0.3.
